title: The Dark Arts of Web Automation: Teaching Agents to Use Websites Like Humans — Corey Gallon, Rexmore
talk_summary: Corey Gallon demonstrates driving a real Chrome browser via the DevTools Protocol (CDP) from a CLI rather than an MCP server, using a sense-act-verify loop and a three-rung 'meatbag ladder' (synthetic JS click → trusted CDP input → humanlike motion/vision) to automate hostile web UIs and even CAPTCHAs. The key architectural lesson is splitting deterministic code (fast, free, reusable) from the agent (only the vision/thinking steps), which is dramatically cheaper and faster than round-tripping a model on every interaction.

takeaways.technique: CLI over MCP for deterministic tool sequences
takeaways.what_they_do: Give agents shell-based CLI tools instead of MCP servers so a solved interaction sequence can be replayed as a program without a model in the loop on every step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP took 71 round trips and 8 minutes for the same task that took a CLI only seven turns and in under one minute.
takeaways.numbers: CLI vs MCP: ~83% success both; MCP 71 round trips / 8 min vs CLI 7 turns / <1 min; up to 75x cheaper token cost (Anthropic)

takeaways.what_they_do: Pure code does all deterministic driving (clicks, retries, rearming on expiry); the agent is only called for the one step needing eyes/brain (reading a grid), then idles until next call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Code does the deterministic driving and the agent does the only bits that require eyes and a brain.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the loop manually to find a working path, then persist it as code and/or an agent skill so it never has to be rediscovered.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You write the solution down so you never have to figure it out again. And you write it down as code or as an agent skill or very often as both.

takeaways.technique: Verify through a different channel than the action
takeaways.what_they_do: After acting, confirm success by sensing through a different channel (network/screen) rather than trusting the action's own return value.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you've clicked something, don't ask the click if it was successful. Check the network or check the screen.

takeaways.what_they_do: Start with the cheapest/fastest method (synthetic JS click) and only escalate to more expensive humanlike methods when the page rejects it.
